newsitem.title: USA: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer weighing IPO timing - Variety.
newsitem.headline: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer weighing IPO timing - Variety.

text.p: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc (MGM) has been talking with Wall Street firms to try to set the best time for an initial public offering, and could go public as early as the fourth quarter, Daily Variety said.
Variety said in its Friday edition that MGM executives had meet recently with bankers from J.P. Morgan & Co Inc, Bear Stearns Cos Inc, Merrill Lynch and Co Inc and Goldman Sachs.
As part of its review, MGM has looked at the debt markets and the private equity markets as well as the timing of a public stock offering, Variety said.

Several unnamed bankers involved said it was evident that no decision had been made about taking MGM public, but people close to the company acknowledged that a stock offering was now more likely to occur sooner than previously thought.

Unnamed sources told Variety that the $573 million acquisition of Orion Pictures had accelerated the possible timing of an offering because the acquisition will increase MGM's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation, making it more attractive to investors.
However, there appeared to be different opinions about the matter among MGM executives, Variety said.
"There are several different decision-making bodies here and not everybody is on the same page," one person familiar with the talks said.
The decision will be made by MGM's two shareholders, Kirk Kerkorian's Tracinda Corp and Australia's Seven Network Ltd, as well as by the management team led by Chairman Frank Mancuso.
